steps.title: Confirm Diagnosis
steps.instructions: Perform malaria rapid diagnostic test (mRDT) or blood smear. All suspected malaria cases MUST have parasitological confirmation before treatment.
warningFlags: Do NOT treat presumptively if RDT available

steps.title: Classify Severity
steps.instructions: Check for danger signs: inability to drink/breastfeed, persistent vomiting, convulsions, lethargy/unconsciousness, inability to sit/stand.
steps.escalation: If ANY red flag present → Refer immediately as SEVERE MALARIA

steps.title: Treatment — Adults & Children >5kg
steps.instructions: First-line: Artemether-Lumefantrine (AL) for 3 days. Give with fatty food to improve absorption.

medications.name: Artemether-Lumefantrine
medications.frequency: Twice daily (0, 8, 24, 36, 48, 60 hours) = 6 doses over 3 days

steps.title: Follow-up
steps.instructions: Review on Day 3 if symptoms persist. Repeat mRDT on Day 3 if still febrile. If treatment failure, switch to second-line ACT.

steps.title: Emergency Stabilization
steps.instructions: Establish IV access. Check glucose (hypoglycemia common). Manage airway. Monitor vitals every 15 minutes.

steps.title: Pre-Referral Treatment
steps.instructions: If IV artesunate not available at facility, give pre-referral treatment and REFER IMMEDIATELY.

medications.name: Artesunate IV/IM
medications.duration: Until oral medication tolerated (minimum 24 hours IV)

medications.name: Artesunate rectal (pre-referral)
medications.indication: Pre-referral only when injection not possible

steps.title: Referral
steps.instructions: All severe malaria cases should be managed at a facility with inpatient capacity. Refer urgently with documentation of pre-referral treatment given.

steps.title: Assess for HIV Testing
steps.instructions: Offer HIV testing to: all patients with TB symptoms, all pregnant women, STI patients, all patients who request it. Use opt-out approach in high-prevalence settings.

steps.title: Perform Testing
steps.instructions: Use national testing algorithm. Typically: rapid test 1 → if reactive, rapid test 2 (different manufacturer). If discordant, send for confirmatory test.

steps.title: If HIV Positive
steps.instructions: Post-test counseling. Assess for WHO clinical staging and CD4 count. Initiate ART same day if clinically ready (Treat All approach). Screen for TB, hepatitis B, STIs.

steps.title: If HIV Negative
steps.instructions: Post-test counseling on risk reduction. If high-risk exposure in last 72 hours, consider PEP. If ongoing high risk, consider PrEP. Retest in 3 months if in window period.

steps.title: TB Symptom Screen
steps.instructions: Ask about the 4 cardinal symptoms: cough ≥2 weeks, fever, night sweats, weight loss. In HIV-positive patients, ANY one symptom is sufficient to warrant investigation.

steps.title: Investigate
steps.instructions: Collect 2 sputum samples (spot + early morning). Send for GeneXpert MTB/RIF as first-line test. Chest X-ray if available.

steps.title: Treatment — New TB Case
steps.instructions: Start standard 6-month regimen: 2 months intensive phase + 4 months continuation phase. Register in TB register. Notify public health.

steps.title: Treatment Monitoring
steps.instructions: Monthly reviews: weight, symptom assessment, medication adherence. Sputum at months 2, 5, 6. If sputum positive at month 2, extend intensive phase and request drug sensitivity testing.

steps.title: Confirm Diagnosis
steps.instructions: Diagnosis requires elevated BP on at least 2 separate occasions. Measure BP in both arms at first visit. Use appropriate cuff size. Patient should be seated, resting for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment
steps.instructions: Assess total CV risk: age, sex, smoking, diabetes, cholesterol, family history. Check for target organ damage: proteinuria, LVH, retinopathy.

steps.title: Lifestyle Modifications (All Patients)
steps.instructions: Reduce salt intake (<5g/day). Regular physical activity (30 min/day, 5 days/week). Healthy diet (fruits, vegetables, reduce fat). Limit alcohol. Stop smoking. Maintain healthy weight (BMI 18.5-24.9).

steps.title: Pharmacological Treatment
steps.instructions: Start medication if: Stage 1 with high CV risk or target organ damage, or Stage 2+, or diabetes/CKD with BP ≥130/80.

medications.name: Amlodipine
medications.indication: First-line, especially in Black African patients

medications.name: Enalapril
medications.indication: First-line if diabetes/proteinuria. NOT in pregnancy.

medications.name: Hydrochlorothiazide
medications.indication: Add-on or first-line if fluid overload/heart failure

steps.title: Hypertensive Crisis
steps.instructions: If SBP ≥180 or DBP ≥120 with symptoms (headache, visual changes, chest pain, dyspnea): This is a hypertensive EMERGENCY. Give sublingual nifedipine 10mg, monitor closely, REFER to hospital.

steps.title: Confirm Diagnosis
steps.instructions: Fasting plasma glucose ≥7.0 mmol/L (126 mg/dL) on 2 occasions, OR random glucose ≥11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) with symptoms, OR HbA1c ≥6.5% (48 mmol/mol).

steps.title: Baseline Assessment
steps.instructions: Full history and examination. Check for complications: eyes (retinopathy), feet (neuropathy, ulcers), kidneys (proteinuria), cardiovascular risk.

steps.title: Lifestyle Modifications (All Patients)
steps.instructions: Dietary counseling: reduce refined carbohydrates, increase fiber, regular meals. Physical activity: 150 min/week moderate intensity. Weight management. Smoking cessation. Foot care education.

steps.title: Pharmacological Treatment
steps.instructions: Start Metformin if lifestyle measures insufficient after 3 months (or immediately if HbA1c >8%). Target HbA1c <7% for most adults.

medications.name: Metformin
medications.dose: Start 500 mg daily, increase to 500 mg BD, max 1g BD
medications.indication: First-line for all T2DM. Take with meals to reduce GI side effects.

medications.name: Glimepiride
medications.indication: Add if HbA1c >7% on max metformin. WARN about hypoglycemia.

medications.name: Insulin (NPH)
medications.dose: Start 10 units at bedtime, titrate by 2 units every 3 days to target FPG <7
medications.indication: If dual oral therapy fails, or HbA1c >10%, or symptomatic hyperglycemia

steps.title: Diabetic Emergencies
steps.instructions: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA): glucose >14, ketones positive, acidotic breathing. Hyperosmolar state: glucose >33, altered consciousness. BOTH are emergencies requiring immediate IV fluids and insulin. REFER to hospital.

steps.title: Check for General Danger Signs
steps.instructions: Ask: Is the child able to drink/breastfeed? Does the child vomit everything? Has the child had convulsions? Look: Is the child lethargic or unconscious?
steps.escalation: ANY danger sign → Give pre-referral treatment → REFER URGENTLY

steps.title: Assess Fever
steps.instructions: Temperature ≥37.5°C or feels hot. Check: Duration of fever. History of measles in last 3 months. Stiff neck. Bulging fontanelle (infants). Rash.

steps.title: Classify and Treat
steps.instructions: VERY SEVERE FEBRILE DISEASE: Danger sign + fever → First dose antibiotics + antimalarial + refer. MALARIA: Positive RDT → ACT for 3 days. FEVER — MALARIA UNLIKELY: Negative RDT + no other cause → Paracetamol, review in 2 days.

medications.name: Paracetamol
medications.indication: All febrile children for symptomatic relief

steps.title: Counsel Mother/Caregiver
steps.instructions: When to return immediately: unable to drink/breastfeed, becomes sicker, fever persists >3 days, develops convulsions. Extra fluids. Continue feeding. Use insecticide-treated nets.

steps.title: Assess Dehydration
steps.instructions: Look: general condition (well/restless/lethargic), eyes (normal/sunken), skin pinch (returns quickly/slowly/very slowly). Ask: Is the child thirsty?

criteria.Some dehydration: 2+ signs (restless, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, slow skin pinch): Plan B
criteria.Severe dehydration: 2+ signs (lethargic, sunken eyes, unable to drink, very slow pinch): Plan C

steps.title: Plan A — Treat at Home
steps.instructions: Give extra fluids (as much as child will take). Give ORS after each loose stool: <2 yrs: 50-100ml; 2-10 yrs: 100-200ml; >10 yrs: as much as wanted. Give zinc supplements. Continue feeding.

medications.name: ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts)
medications.dose: 50-100 ml per loose stool (<2 yrs), 100-200 ml (2-10 yrs)

steps.title: Plan B — Treat at Facility
steps.instructions: Give ORS over 4 hours: weight(kg) × 75 ml. Reassess after 4 hours and reclassify. If improving → Plan A. If same → repeat Plan B. If worsening → Plan C.

steps.title: Plan C — Severe Dehydration
steps.instructions: Start IV Ringer's Lactate immediately. If IV not possible, refer urgently with ORS by mouth/NG tube en route.

medications.name: Ringer's Lactate IV
medications.dose: Infant: 30 ml/kg over 1 hr, then 70 ml/kg over 5 hrs. Older child: 30 ml/kg over 30 min, then 70 ml/kg over 2.5 hrs

referralCriteria: Signs of cholera in outbreak area

steps.title: Bloody Diarrhea (Dysentery)
steps.instructions: If blood in stool: treat as dysentery with ciprofloxacin. Follow up in 2 days. If not improving, consider amebic dysentery (metronidazole).

steps.title: Assess for Pneumonia
steps.instructions: Count respiratory rate for full 60 seconds (child must be calm). Check: chest indrawing, stridor when calm, oxygen saturation.

criteria.Chest indrawing: Lower chest wall draws in on inspiration

steps.title: Classify
steps.instructions: SEVERE PNEUMONIA: Chest indrawing OR danger sign → Give first dose antibiotics → REFER. PNEUMONIA: Fast breathing, no chest indrawing → Oral amoxicillin. NO PNEUMONIA (COUGH/COLD): No fast breathing, no indrawing → Safe home care.

steps.title: Pre-Referral — Severe Pneumonia
steps.instructions: Give first dose of both antibiotics. Keep child warm. If SpO2 <90%, give oxygen. REFER URGENTLY to hospital.

steps.title: First ANC Visit (Before 12 Weeks Ideally)
steps.instructions: Confirm pregnancy. Calculate gestational age and EDD. Full history and examination. Blood pressure, weight, height.

medications.name: Ferrous sulfate + Folic acid
medications.dose: 60 mg elemental iron + 400 mcg folic acid daily

steps.title: Routine ANC Visits Schedule
steps.instructions: WHO recommends minimum 8 contacts: Weeks 12, 20, 26, 30, 34, 36, 38, 40. Each visit: BP, weight, fundal height, fetal heart rate, urinalysis for proteinuria.

steps.title: IPT for Malaria (Endemic Areas)
steps.instructions: Give intermittent preventive treatment with SP from 13 weeks. At least 3 doses, 1 month apart. Give as DOT (directly observed therapy).

medications.name: Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (SP/Fansidar)
medications.frequency: Monthly from 13 weeks to delivery (minimum 3 doses)

steps.title: Obstetric Danger Signs — REFER
steps.instructions: Educate mother on danger signs requiring immediate facility visit.

steps.title: Diagnosis
steps.instructions: History of recurrent episodes of wheeze, cough (especially at night/early morning), chest tightness, breathlessness. Symptoms variable, triggered by exercise/allergens/infections. Peak flow variability >20%.

steps.title: Acute Asthma Attack
steps.instructions: Assess severity: mild (talks in sentences), moderate (talks in phrases), severe (talks in words), life-threatening (silent chest, drowsy).

medications.name: Salbutamol inhaler (MDI + spacer)
medications.dose: 4-8 puffs, repeat every 20 min for 1 hour if needed

steps.title: Long-term Management
steps.instructions: Step-up approach. All patients need a reliever (salbutamol). Add controller (inhaled corticosteroid) if symptoms frequent. Teach inhaler technique. Written asthma action plan.

medications.name: Beclomethasone inhaler
medications.dose: Low dose: 100-200 mcg BD; Medium: 200-400 mcg BD
medications.indication: Controller — start if symptoms >2x/week or any nighttime symptoms

steps.title: Wound Assessment
steps.instructions: Assess: type (laceration/abrasion/puncture/crush), depth, contamination, time since injury, tendon/nerve/vessel involvement, foreign bodies.

steps.title: Clean & Irrigate
steps.instructions: Copious irrigation with clean water or normal saline. Remove visible debris and foreign bodies. Debride devitalized tissue. Clean wound with antiseptic (povidone-iodine or chlorhexidine).

steps.title: Tetanus Prophylaxis
steps.instructions: Check immunization status. Clean minor wound: TT if >10 years since last dose. Tetanus-prone wound (dirty, >6 hrs, deep/puncture): TT if >5 years + consider TIG if incomplete/unknown primary series.

steps.title: Treatment & Closure
steps.instructions: Primary closure if: clean wound <6 hours old (face: up to 24 hrs). Delayed primary closure: contaminated wounds, >6 hours. Leave open: infected/heavily contaminated wounds, bite wounds.

medications.name: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate
medications.dose: Adults: 625 mg TDS; Children: 25 mg/kg/day divided TDS
medications.indication: Only for: bite wounds, crush injuries, heavy contamination, immunocompromised patients
